newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CPFL plans to buy power from five plants.
newsitem.headline: CPFL plans to buy power from five plants.

text.p: Sao Paulo state power firm Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) said it plans to buy 193,544 megawatts (MWh) of electrical energy from five sugar- and alcohol-fueled power plants.

In a statement, CPFL said it is negotiating purchase agreements with generators in the Ribeirao Preto area, which would feed electricity to the company's distribution network following the 1999 harvest.
"We invited bids and got five partners," CPFL operations director Jose Carlos Bottesi was quoted as saying.
One requirement regarding the sale was to establish a minimum block per plant of 8 MW of power, the statement said.
The five generating plants were identified as Jardest S.A., Usina Junqueira, Usina A.A. MB Ltda, Usina Bomfim and Usina da Pedra.
The technical aspects of their proposals are still being studied by CPFL, the statement said.
